33.steps:
1. Clear the log (post action "clearLogNow").
  3. Issue 10 pings from 10 different LAN-side IP addresses. Verify that encrypted SSO requests for the 10 source IP addresses are generated and reply to them.
  4. Wait for an SSO poll message after 1 minute. This message contains 10 user IP addresses. Reply to it sending a separate message for each user. Each message contains User IP address/User name.
  5. Retrieve log.csv and verify that a "user logged in" event for each user was logged. Retrieve the TSR and verify that in the Users section under Users currently connected 10 users are reported as logged in.
  6. Wait for an SSO poll message after 1 minute. Reply to it sending messages for 9 users.
  7. Repeat step 6. Retrieve the TSR and verify that in the Users section under Users currently connected all 10 users are reported as logged in.
  8. Wait for next SSO poll message.
33.initial:
1. Configure SSO with an agent at IP address on the LAN.
  2. Set the SSO agent timeout to 5 seconds and retries to 2.
  3. Set the mechanism for setting user group memberships to "local configuration".
  4. Set the SSO polling rate and hold time after failure both to 1 minute.
  5. Create a local user group "group1" who is a member of Trusted Users.
  6. Create a local user "user1" who is a member of "group1".
  7. Create a local user "user2" who is not a member of "group1".
  8. Set the default LAN>WAN access rule "Users Allowed" to "group1".
33.title: The order of IP addresses in multi-user request in SSO polling.
33.result: The IP address of the user who has not been heard from after several polls comes first in an SSO poll message.
